Rafflesia 
(Rafflesia spp.) 

A parasitic plant famed for producing some of the world's largest, most bizarre flowers, Rafflesia has no true roots, stems or leaves, and lives entirely inside jungle vines (Tetrastigma) until it blooms into a massive, flesh-coloured flower that mimics the scent of rotting flesh to attract pollinators. Because Rafflesia relies on a specific host vine and extremely delicate microclimates, even minor forest degradation can wipe out local populations. The tribe's absolute ban on human intrusion and harvesting within the 319-acre core watershed will shield the fragile plants from being destroyed.
